Tool Use & Function Calling

Giving eyes, ears, and hands to LLMs. The bridge between text generation and real-world action.

JSON Schema Definition

Modern models (GPT-4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) are fine-tuned to output structured JSON when tools are defined. The standard format is a list of tool definitions including name, description, and parameters (JSON Schema). 

{
  "name": "get_stock_price",
  "description": "Get current stock price for a ticker",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "ticker": {"type": "string", "description": "e.g. AAPL"},
      "currency": {"type": "string", "enum": ["USD", "EUR"]}
    },
    "required": ["ticker"]
  }
}

Parallel Tool Calling

Advanced agents can call multiple tools in a single turn. For example, if asked "Compare weather in NY and London," the model can output a list of tool calls: [get_weather(NY), get_weather(London)]. These are executed in parallel, reducing latency.

sequenceDiagram participant User participant LLM participant ToolHost User->>LLM: "Get price of BTC and ETH" LLM->>ToolHost: "Call: [get_price(BTC), get_price(ETH)]" ToolHost->>ToolHost: Execute Parallel ToolHost->>LLM: "Results: [98000, 2700]" LLM->>User: "BTC is 98k and ETH is 2.7k"

Error Handling

Real-world tool use is messy. APIs fail, timeouts happen. Robust agents must handle:

  • Validation Errors: If the model outputs bad JSON, feed the error message back to the model so it can self-correct.
  • No Result: If a search returns 0 results, the agent should try a broader query.
